situation:
You are a young worker raising a younger sibling on one income, and you earn $2,450 a month after taxes. This morning you have a free appointment with a financial coach (judge) at CLEARWATER COMMUNITY MONEY CENTER, a nonprofit that helps households plan what they spend.

In January your sibling spent a night in the emergency room and you paid $1,900 out of pocket to meet the deductible on your health plan. That payment emptied your savings. Rent, utilities, insurance and a bus pass take a fixed $1,780 a month, and groceries and other variable costs take most of what remains.

Last week the washing machine stopped draining. Buying a new mid-range washer from a dealer costs $660 on a store credit card that charges no interest for six months, allows a twenty-five day grace period, and adds a $39 late fee to any payment that arrives after it. The $110 monthly payment fits this month.

Next month your car insurance premium of $310 comes due on the same date. Buying a used washer from a resale shop costs $240 in cash, carries no warranty, and may fail again within two years. The coach (judge) wants a monthly budget that separates necessary from desired spending, what you looked into before choosing a machine, and your recommendation.

The coach (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the coach's questions, the coach (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are a financial coach at CLEARWATER COMMUNITY MONEY CENTER. Business background is the same as the situation above.

A young worker who is raising a sibling on one income has come in after a broken washing machine, with savings already emptied by a medical deductible paid in January. You want to hear a monthly budget that separates necessary from desired spending, what this worker looked into before choosing a machine, and a clear recommendation on how to replace it.

After the participant has presented, you are to ask the following questions of each participant:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, what would tell you this was the right call?
What would you check each month to know the plan is working?
